modern: To my own free will the free will of my neighbour is just as indifferent as his poor breath and flesh. For though we are made especially for the sake of one another, still the ruling power of each of us has its own office; otherwise my neighbour’s wickedness would be my harm, which God has not willed, so that my unhappiness may not depend on another.

explained.summary: Your neighbour’s choices are as much outside you as their breath and body. We’re made for each other’s sake, yet each mind has its own work and its own responsibility. Otherwise someone else’s wrongdoing would be your harm, and nature has arranged things so that your happiness doesn’t depend on anyone else.
explained.today: Your partner’s bad mood, your teenager’s choices, a colleague’s laziness: you can care, help and speak up, but your own peace isn’t hostage to them.
